entry.title: Wiping and dusting together
entry.summary: Offer a cloth for wiping or dusting alongside you, with help when your child needs it.
entry.cue: Notice your child copying a wiping or sweeping movement or asking to join you.
detail: Keep the cloth or hand mitt where the task happens, with help ready. For an interested child, Davies also describes a manageable broom and dustpan, with a marked place to gather the dirt.
The point is joining the work. It will often be slower and less thorough, and you can stop before either of you feels overwhelmed. Returning the cloth can be a shared last step.

ageContext.bookAge: Wiping spills:12–18 months in the chart; cleaning caption: from 12 months. Appendix dusting/sweeping:16–18+ months; table wiping: once a child can walk.
ageContext.readiness: Interest in copying wiping or cleaning and a tool the child can manage.
ageContext.note: A cloth and shared wiping are the earlier parts. Sweeping and dusting have later appendix labels and can wait for interest and manageable movement. Age and readiness sources: The Montessori Toddler, PDF pp. 14, 64, 246.

displayContext.footer: You don’t need a different home. Start with what you have.
